text.p: Nomura Equity Research downgraded the stocks in Hungary's gas distributor Primagaz Rt to 'hold' from 'buy' and reduced its earnings per share (EPS) forecast too.

"Sales growth is now slowing, however, and although profits growth will continue we have reduced our 1997 EPS forecast from 611 forints to 558 forints," analysts Frances Cloud and Barry MacCarthy said in a company update.
"On this basis we are downgrading our recommendation from buy to hold," they said.
Nomura said that Primagaz's turnover growth will slow in 1997 as the company reduces the pace of expansion of its bulk business in order to focus on higher quality customers.
Nomura expected Primagaz's sales to rise to 22.72 billion forints in 1997, up 29 percent from 17.62 billion in 1996. Last year the company's sales rose 42.7 percent.
In February's Primagaz's CEO Zoltan Szemmelveisz said the company planned to boost its sales to 22 billion in 1997.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Primagaz shares closed unchanged at 10,000 forints.
